summary: Lancaster County state tower; built in the 1939-40 report year, replaced by a steel structure in 1957-58, sold at auction in 2010, and marked removed.

facts.status_note: The Eastern US Lookouts record marks the tower as Removed. The record gives no removal date.

events.note: A new tower was constructed at the Riverside site. The state commission report covers July 1939 to June 1940.
The old wooden tower was replaced by a new steel structure. The state commission report covers July 1957 to June 1958.
The tower was sold at auction. The record gives no buyer, price or location.

evidence.supports: Riverside tower is in Lancaster County
Agency is the South Carolina Forestry Commission
A new tower was constructed at the Riverside site in the 1939-40 report year
evidence.quote: A new tower was constructed at the Riverside tower site in Lancaster County.

evidence.supports: The Civilian Conservation Corps built fire towers and telephone lines at no cost to the state
evidence.quote: All fire towers, tower buildings and telephone line construction was done by the Civilian Conservation Corps at no cost to the State or protective associations.

evidence.supports: Old wooden tower replaced by a new steel structure in 1957-58
evidence.quote: 1957-58: The old wooden tower located at Riverside was replaced by a new steel structure. (Report of the State Commission of Forestry, 7/1/57 to 6/30/58)
2010: The tower was sold at auction.

evidence.supports: Record marks the tower as removed
Towers were the public's point of contact for reporting fires and linked to firefighters
evidence.quote: Towers were the public's fire reporting contact point, and served as the communications link for firefighters in the field.

evidence.supports: Commission closed its fire tower system on October 1, 1993
evidence.quote: The Forestry Commission closed its fire tower system on October 1, 1993.

evidence.supports: State was selling a number of its towers; AP story dated February 28, 2006
evidence.quote: The state is selling a number of the towers.

evidence.supports: Forestry Commission closed the last tower in 1993
evidence.quote: The Forestry Commission oversees the towers and closed the last one in 1993.

notes_for_editor: The Eastern US Lookouts page quotes state commission reports for 1939-40, 1957-58 and 2010. The reports themselves were not read. The 2010 auction is one line with no buyer or location. Searches for an auction record for this tower found nothing specific. The WIS AP story from February 2006 is background only and does not name this tower. Riverside Fire Department in Lancaster is a different, active department and is not linked to this tower.
